claims.text: As-cast equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi lacks nanoscale chemical clustering.
As-cast equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi lacks nanoscale precipitates.
The absence of clustering or precipitation produces a homogeneous, dislocation-friendly solid solution.
The homogeneous solid solution permits easy dislocation glide.
Easy dislocation glide accounts for the alloy's favorable plasticity and machinability.
The homogeneous solid solution limits work hardening and intrinsic lattice friction, resulting in relatively low hardness and strength.
The starting material is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% each of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti.
The starting alloy is an as-cast, single-phase simple solid solution.
The starting alloy has a random atomic distribution.
A controlled thermal treatment or minor alloying modification can induce nanoscale chemical ordering or precipitation without forming deleterious intermetallic phases.
Nanoscale precipitates or chemically ordered clusters act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
A uniformly random atomic distribution minimizes local lattice strain and lowers barriers to dislocation motion.
Introducing nanoscale clusters increases dislocation pinning and lattice friction.
Increased dislocation pinning and lattice friction enhance hardness and yield strength while reducing ductility.
A successfully treated or subtly modified alloy will have greater hardness than the as-cast alloy.
A successfully treated or subtly modified alloy will have greater yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
The increase in hardness and yield strength will coincide with nanoscale precipitates or chemical short-range order detectable by microstructural characterization.
The proposed effect applies near the equimolar CoCrFeNiTi composition and from approximately 25 °C to 600 °C under tensile or compressive loading.
Coarse or excessive precipitation may produce brittleness instead of a favorable strength-ductility balance.
A controlled comparison of as-cast and heat-treated equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can test whether ordering or precipitation causes changes in hardness, yield strength, and ductility.

contradictions.description: The rule treats failure of the treatment to produce ordering or precipitates as falsification, but the causal hypothesis requires that mediator to be induced. Failure to create the mediator is an intervention failure, not a decisive test of whether the mediator would strengthen the alloy.
